There is very little known about this 'tank' What information is made public is that it was manufactured by the German Reich some time during the war, and shipped to then Japanese held territory in Manchuria. In 1945 it was captured by the Soviets, according to them no documentation was found with it. It had a single drive dieseal engine which was stripped out during reverse engineering of the prototype. side view.

At some point when the Soviets were satisfied with the information they were able to learn from the vehicle it was shipped to the Kubinka tank museum in Moscow, but it was essentially hidden behind another display for many years. Relatively recently it has obtained its own display and all requests to obtain a sample of the metal have been denied. Whether this is routine or not I cannot say. Apparently the metal is armor is approximately 5mm thick.

On a side note on something I've noticed, there are a great deal of prototype and German weaponry in Russian museums especially in the Kubinka tank museum. All of them come with a plethora of detail and information. This piece in particular seems to be almost totally devoid of any details beyond those written on the display placard.

There are many articles surrounding this vehicle online pointing out the lack of details and Russian refusal of the metal sample. And of course this has lead to many theories from it being an 'unknown metal' not known to the world today to it being an alien design with people often pointing out that the Germans kept amazing records and to find something with none is strange.

I'm trying to make it a rule to not give an opinion on such things but in this case I will. I highly doubt either of these theories are true from the basic fact that this thing is on display at all. It would be a ridiculous decision to have it on display at all even if it was a facsimile of the real 'alien' or 'unknown metal' vehicle.

Furthermore, the design reminds me of several early WW1 German Empire prototype vehicles. Also the fact that the documentation was lost in Manchuria is really not surprising considering the mess that Manchuria had become near the end of the war. Like many documents at the time the info was likely destroyed during a bombing raid or fire. Like many prototype vehicles we see during both WWI and WWII the vehicles tended to become stranger and stranger as the end of both wars neared as desperation no doubt kicked in for the losing sides.
